newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market inactive - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market inactive - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade was quiet following brisk sales last week at $66.00 per cwt, feedlot sources said.
Light bids at $65.00 were countered by owners seeking $67.00 to $68.00.
Early outlooks for steady to firm fed cattle prices were tied to ideas momentum from last week's $2.00 advance would continue, the sources said.
Last week's gains were spurred by a steep increase in beef prices and perceptions that market-ready cattle supplies would start declining into the fall, they said.

Beef prices at midday were quoted mixed in sluggish movement, with heavyweight choice beef at $108.86 per cwt, down $0.01, USDA reported. There were 47 fabricated beef loads sold. Heavyweight choice beef gained $4.10 last week, but slipped on Friday.
Several market sources speculated that beef prices had topped and were now poised to drop.
"I can see beef (heavyweight choice) coming off $2.00 this week," said Dave Maher, analyst with Securities Corp of Iowa.
Maher added that a slowdown in beef movement suggested the higher prices were stifling retail demand.
